original_card.question: Can one known scalar simplification be converted into an actual paid-profile improvement?
methods: Derive the changed legal frame itinerary and exact child histogram.
Prove a scoped obstruction showing why that scalar gain cannot change the paid contract.
original_card.acceptance_gate: An unchanged histogram is not a kappa gain; record any separate runtime or proof benefit explicitly.

first_step.inspect: Observe that the positive control improves scalar counts while retaining the paid histogram.
first_step.scope: Positive control / source-bound orientation only; this is not a new construction or full cold replay.

original_card.first_experiment: Choose one simplification and derive the complete changed frame itinerary, or prove why it cannot change the histogram.
original_card.bottleneck_link: A legal change to the histogram, not addition count alone, is the bridge to an exponent gain.
allowed_variations: One existing scalar simplification and one proposed frame-path change.
scope_change_triggers: Submitting only another scalar count as completion of a paid-profile task.

actual_scope: Independently check the interaction and new-gap reductions for the radius-one fixed-frame two-ADD class on both pinned PR3734 providers, including exhaustive first-frame coverage.
scope_change_reason: The card asks for one scalar simplification's paid histogram. PR #3942 already certifies that this two-ADD class does not improve the raw rank moment, and its released handoff asks for an independent challenge of the reduction rather than another census. This package answers that review. A missed legal interior price would be a scalar move whose histogram was never tested.
bottleneck_link: A two-ADD retiming changes the exponent only if its rank histogram improves. Confirming that every legal fixed-frame interior price is either an old single-move price or one of the four losing bridge rows blocks that scalar route from being recounted as a paid-profile gain.
stop_rule: Stop after both providers' fixed-frame interior prices and radius-one frame intervals are checked. Do not replay the 11917718 variable-frame second-move rows or search a longer first displacement.
evidence: Both providers: 4709 fixed pairs, 14966 scalar-legal bridge gates, 14693 bridge dimensions, max quotient rank 3, and the same four losing restore rows published by PR #3942. No omitted interior price and no bridge-formula mismatch. One-vector subspace counts match the Gaussian binomials on all 1292 intervals.
author: unpaidmoon
ai_assistance: Cursor Grok 4.7 wrote the independent checker and the package text. The predecessor trace oracle and both provider words are unchanged bytes from PR #3942.

open_questions.question: Does every changed-frame first ADD, followed by every legal second ADD on a disjoint register set, have combined raw-moment delta equal to the sum of two original single-move deltas?
open_questions.why_it_matters: PROOF.md section 2 uses that identity to skip the disjoint pairs. This package checks only the crossing algebra, not the summed histograms.
open_questions.first_step: Reprice one changed-frame first word against the frozen single-move receipt, restricted to ADDs whose touched sets miss the moved gate.
open_questions.blocked_by: The variable-frame census is about 11.9 million rows and is outside this review's stop rule.

open_questions.question: Does selecting the same ADD twice always collapse to an original single-ADD candidate on every radius-one first move?
open_questions.why_it_matters: That is the other half of the interaction reduction. A failed undo would be a word the census does not price.
open_questions.first_step: Apply one radius-one move and its inverse on every changed first frame, and compare the restored gate list.
open_questions.blocked_by: Needs the variable first-move list. The fixed-frame class checked here does not move a frame, so the same-gate case is a different branch.
